name: Reverse Engineering
summary: Disassemblers, debuggers and analysis tools for binaries and firmware
description: Static and dynamic analysis of binaries, libraries, firmware and mobile apps: debuggers, decompilers, tracers, hex editors, ELF/PE inspection, emulation and fuzzing. For malware analysis, run samples only inside an isolated lab (see the lab-setup guide). Ghidra, radare2 and Cutter are not in Debian main and are listed as external tools with install links.

external.name: Ghidra
external.summary: Full-featured software reverse-engineering suite and decompiler
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source), released by the NSA; not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Ghidra is free and open source but ships as a large self-contained Java release and is not packaged in Debian; it needs a JDK, which SHADOW can install.

how.text: Download the official release archive from the Ghidra site, extract it, and run ghidraRun; a JDK (e.g. Debian's default-jdk) is required.

external.name: radare2 / Cutter
external.summary: Reverse-engineering framework (radare2) and its Qt GUI (Cutter)
external.license: LGPL-3.0 (radare2) and GPL-3.0 (Cutter); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: radare2 and Cutter are free software but are not in Debian trixie; upstream recommends their own installers for current versions.

how.text: Install radare2 from its official git checkout (sys/install.sh), and Cutter from the official AppImage or release build.

external.name: Frida
external.summary: Dynamic instrumentation toolkit for hooking running processes
external.license: wxWindows/LGPL-style (open source), distributed on PyPI; not in Debian.

why.text: Frida ships prebuilt native components per platform through PyPI and is not packaged in Debian.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx (pipx install frida-tools); matching gadget/server binaries come from the Frida releases page.

external.name: IDA Free
external.summary: Freeware edition of the IDA interactive disassembler

why.text: IDA Free is closed-source and cannot be redistributed by Shadow OS.

how.text: Download the installer for Linux from Hex-Rays and accept the licence.

external.name: x64dbg
external.summary: Open-source x64/x32 debugger for Windows binaries
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); Windows-only, not packaged in Debian.

why.text: x64dbg is a Windows application; on Shadow OS it runs under Wine and is not in Debian.

how.text: Download the official snapshot and run it under Wine (wine is in Debian).

external.name: jadx
external.summary: Decompile Android DEX/APK to readable Java source
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: jadx is a Java/Gradle application released as archives and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Download the official release archive and run bin/jadx or bin/jadx-gui; a JDK (in Debian) is required.

external.name: objection
external.summary: Runtime mobile exploration powered by Frida
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: objection is published on PyPI/GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install objection').

external.name: MobSF
external.summary: Mobile Security Framework for static and dynamic app analysis
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: MobSF is a Django web application usually deployed with Docker and is not in Debian.

how.text: Run the official Docker image, or set it up from the git checkout per the MobSF docs.

external.name: drozer
external.summary: Android security assessment and IPC testing framework
external.license: BSD-3-Clause (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: drozer is published as release packages on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install the official release package or use pipx; pair it with the drozer agent APK.

external.name: capa
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: capa is published on PyPI and as standalone binaries by Mandiant, and is not in Debian.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install flare-capa'), or download a standalone binary.

external.name: FLOSS
external.summary: Automatically extract obfuscated strings from malware
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: FLOSS is published on PyPI and as standalone binaries by Mandiant, and is not in Debian.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install flare-floss'), or download a standalone binary.

external.name: PE-bear
external.summary: Reversing-oriented viewer and editor for PE files
external.license: BSD-2-Clause (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: PE-bear is distributed as release builds on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Download the official Linux release build from the PE-bear releases page.

external.name: Detect It Easy
external.summary: Identify file types, packers and compilers
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Detect It Easy (DIE) is distributed as release builds on GitHub and is not in Debian.

how.text: Download the official Linux release (AppImage or package) from the DIE releases page.

external.name: GEF
external.summary: GDB Enhanced Features for exploit development
external.license: MIT (open source); a GDB extension script, not packaged in Debian.

why.text: GEF is a single Python script that extends GDB and is not packaged in Debian.

how.text: Download gef.py into your home and source it from ~/.gdbinit per the GEF install docs; GDB is in Debian.

external.name: pwndbg
external.summary: Exploit-development and reversing plugin for GDB
external.license: MIT (open source); a GDB plugin, not packaged in Debian.

why.text: pwndbg is a GDB plugin installed from its own setup and is not in Debian.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run ./setup.sh, which wires it into ~/.gdbinit; GDB is in Debian.

external.name: honggfuzz
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: honggfuzz is maintained on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie (AFL++, which is, is an alternative).

how.text: Build from the official source release with 'make'; its build dependencies (binutils, libunwind) are in Debian.
